summary: Review/documentation phase only -- no source behavior changes, no Runtime Context, no execution capability introduced; no file under src/pcae/ touched. A deliberate architectural checkpoint across the nine phases (110A-111D) that built the PCAE Runtime subsystem, before starting the Runtime Context track. Every finding was produced by a runnable check against live source, live CLI output, or live doc text -- direct dir() inspection of RuntimeRegistry/runtime_introspection's public surface, direct reading of every reviewed module's actual import statements, a live pcae runtime --help / pcae --help invocation, and a live PermissionBroker().evaluate() call -- rather than re-summarizing what each prior phase already claimed about itself. Reviews responsibility separation (Runtime, Registry, Plugins, Introspection, Runtime Inspect CLI, Permission Broker, Observation Integration -- no creep found in any, verified against live code surface not documentation), dependency direction (full import graph traced and confirmed acyclic; runtime_registry.py and permission_broker_foundation.py confirmed zero-dependency leaves; broker isolation confirmed), plugin isolation/extensibility (all twelve example future plugins confirmed to map onto the ten already-frozen categories with zero code change required to register their metadata), registry and introspection purity (reconfirmed via direct inspection), Runtime Inspect CLI (output usefulness, JSON stability, machine/human readability, safety all reconfirmed; long-term usefulness for AI agents flagged Medium risk since plugin/capability sections are structurally always empty due to no cross-invocation persistence, a direct correct consequence of 110E's design, not a defect), safety invariants (reconfirmed live including a fresh PermissionBroker().evaluate() call; no invariant has weakened at any point across 110A-111D), and Runtime Context (112A) readiness (Session/Task/Phase have real precedents but are not yet introspection-modeled per 111B's deferral; Intent/Approval/Broker-decision/Evidence have no persistence model at all today, flagged as the central open design question 112A must resolve explicitly). Seven-item risk register, none Blocker: two Strengths (R-2: the ten-category taxonomy comfortably covers all twelve named future plugin types; R-6: the Registry's implementation pattern is a proven, directly reusable template for Runtime Context's new object types) and five Low/Medium risks (R-1: CLI layering leak around Introspection; R-3: manifest exclusion convention lives in CLI layer not Introspection layer; R-4: plugin/capability CLI output structurally always empty; R-5: undesigned persistence for Intent/Approval/Decision/Evidence; R-7: naming overlap with ~30 unrelated pre-existing pcae runtime-* advisory commands). Recommendation: Proceed to 112A, with one condition -- 112A's own phase brief should explicitly require a documented Persistence Model decision for each of Intent, Approval, Broker decision, and Evidence, mirroring 110E's own explicit choice for the Registry. Added docs/PCAE_RUNTIME_ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md, docs/PHASE_111_RUNTIME_ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md. docs/ROADMAP.md evaluated and found to need no change. 143 new tests (tests/test_runtime_architecture_review.py), a pure documentation-verification suite. Focused tests (836), governance/autonomy group (2309), and the release/lifecycle regression subset actually present (1429/1429, excluding the two known-slow phase85/phase87 integration files) all passed under -n auto; fast_green 4390/4390 (matches documented baseline).
